RagShortTexts: The Orsini baronage commanded Castel Sant'Angelo, dominating papal conclaves and Roman.

Variants.Content: Roman baronial power grew upward. Families such as the Orsini fortified towers inside the ruins of antiquity, using imperial monuments as foundations for their walls. Castel Sant'Angelo stood as the most imposing of these strongholds, able to command the Tiber bridge and the approaches to St Peter's. The Orsini aligned with the Guelph cause and the papal curia, and their clients included notaries, bankers and caravan masters who depended on papal contracts. Street fighting between Orsini and Colonna retinues turned whole quarters into battlefields, with crossbowmen firing from upper windows and hired men holding the narrow lanes. Grain, wine and pilgrim offerings moved through markets the rival clans fought to control, since toll gates and granaries paid the men who manned the towers.

A Roman baron measured his worth in towers and in clients. Orsini agents worked the curia, pressing cardinals with promises of castle wardships and revenue from rural estates, while the Colonna rallied their own supporters. A pope who hoped to hold the Lateran had to bargain with these families first, or find his processions blocked at the bridges.
